task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 SECURITY GATE for ISS-0426. Apply your role's INV-1..INV-8 scope test and checks in full. This description names the run-specific risk that makes this review load-bearing rather than routine.

WHY THIS TOUCHES YOUR SCOPE. The change adds two @doc false test-only seams to Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor -- the module implementing REQ-155's LUA-10 layer-2 host-enforced wall-clock kill, which is a SECURITY CONTROL against untrusted tenant scripts. ISS-0426 is a test-infrastructure fix, and its own filing says explicitly: 'DO NOT change Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor's production timeout semantics to fix a test-environment problem -- the wall-clock kill is a security control (LUA-10) and its behaviour under load is the thing being asserted.' Your job is to confirm that boundary held.

THE CENTRAL QUESTION: does adding a test-only bypass of the wall-clock kill to a security-relevant production module create a path by which the control can be evaded in production? Specifically:
  1. run_script_sync/3 and run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 are PUBLIC functions (public with @doc false, not defp). Anything in the codebase -- or any future caller -- can call them, and they do NOT enforce the wall-clock kill. Assess whether that is an acceptable risk as shipped. Consider: is there any production call path that could reach them? Could a future non-test caller reasonably mistake them for the normal entry point? Is @doc false plus a comment sufficient, or does the module need a stronger guard? Note the design considered and rejected a @compile-guarded/test-only -env definition (design section 2.1.1a) -- judge whether that rejection is sound from a SECURITY standpoint specifically, which is a different question from the design ergonomics standpoint it was rejected on.
  2. run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 waits UNBOUNDEDLY (its `after` clause is removed by design). Confirm the max_heap_size: %{kill: true} spawn_opt is retained so the MEMORY limit (REQ-156/LUA-09) still binds, and assess the availability risk of the unbounded wait -- the design's answer is a documented usage contract at executor.ex:601-612 rather than a mechanism. Judge whether a contract is adequate here given these are test-only entry points.
  3. VERIFY -- do not accept -- that production semantics are untouched. ORCH has independently run `git diff main...HEAD --numstat -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex` = 113 insertions, 0 deletions, and confirmed no removed lines at all. Re-derive this yourself and confirm execute_with_manifest/2,3, handle_yield_result/3 and run_with_heap_limit/5's own `after` clause are byte-for-byte unchanged, and that config/config.exs:17's production lua_wallclock_timeout_ms is untouched.
  4. Confirm no tenant-data path, no API route, no migration, and no secrets handling is touched by this change (expected: none -- but confirm rather than assume).

Also assess the tagging change for a security-relevant failure mode: 11 tests that assert the LUA-10 wall-clock kill's behaviour are now EXCLUDED from a default `mix test` run and only execute inside `mix letflow.check.test`'s new isolated subprocess. If that wiring is wrong, the tests asserting a security control would silently stop running anywhere. ELIXIR-DEV reports `mix test --only lua_wallclock_race test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` gives 'Result: 11 passed, 37 excluded'. Verify the tests still execute AND that CI reaches them (ORCH confirmed the chain .github/workflows/ci.yml:126 `mix letflow.check` -> mix.exs alias -> letflow.check.test).

You may READ anything. Do not edit lib/ or test/. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL and per-item verdicts, then commit it to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.

result.summary:
SCOPE TEST: diff touches lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex (a module implementing REQ-155 LUA-10, a security control against untrusted tenant scripts) plus test-only files -- no API route, no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs, no schema/table, no response-shaping code, no lookup-by-ID handler. INV-1 verdict is therefore NOT-APPLICABLE by its own trigger list (no tenant-scoped table/schema/migration in this diff) despite INV-1 being live post-S1/S2 in general -- this specific diff just doesn't touch that surface. Reviewed anyway per the handoff's own framing, since a security-control module is in scope for judgement even when no INV-1..INV-9 trigger literally fires.

PER-INVARIANT VERDICTS (git diff main...HEAD independently re-derived, not accepted from ELIXIR-DEV's report): INV-1 NOT-APPLICABLE (no tenant table/schema/migration touched -- confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD --name-only`, zero priv/repo/migrations files). INV-2 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started, no API response shaping here regardless). INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 sandboxing decision record not yet written; separately, this diff does not touch the sandbox's capability boundary -- see central-question analysis below). INV-4 APPLIES (config-adjacent module) -> PASS: grepped hardcoded-secret pattern against every changed file, zero hits; config/config.exs:17 (lua_wallclock_timeout_ms: 5_000) has an EMPTY diff, confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD -- config/config.exs`. INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started, no lookup-by-ID endpoint). INV-6 APPLIES (new code path in a security-relevant module) -> PASS, this handoff itself is the proof artifact. INV-7 NOT-APPLICABLE (no SQL in this diff). INV-8 APPLIES (executor.ex touched) -> PASS: `grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex` returns exactly one hit, at the pre-existing handle_yield_result/3 clause head (a case-dispatch pattern match against a value the same function's own case already narrowed, not an unresolved external-I/O call) -- unrelated to and unchanged by this diff, not a new violation. INV-9 NOT-APPLICABLE (no outbound HTTP/webhook code here).

RE-DERIVED, NOT ACCEPTED (item 3 of the task): `git diff main...HEAD --numstat -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex` = `113\t0\tlib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex`, matching ORCH's figure exactly -- 113 insertions, 0 deletions, confirmed by reading the full diff text (`git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex`), which shows exactly two new hunks, both pure `+` insertions with zero `-` lines anywhere in the file. Read execute_with_manifest/2 (line 307) and /3 (line 354) directly: both bodies match main verbatim in the diff context (no `-`/`+` inside them). Read handle_yield_result/3's five clauses (lines 669-712): present, unchanged, diff shows zero touches. Read run_with_heap_limit/5 (lines 541-584) directly, including its own `after timeout_ms ->` clause (567-583): present, byte-identical, appears only as unchanged context in the diff. `git diff main...HEAD -- config/config.exs` returns empty output -- confirmed untouched; read config/config.exs:17 directly, it is `config :letflow, lua_wallclock_timeout_ms: 5_000`, matching the design's own claim. `git diff main...HEAD --name-only | grep -E '^lib/'` returns exactly three paths: the design doc, executor.ex, and letflow.check.test.ex -- no other lib/ file touched, confirming item 4 (no tenant-data path, no API route, no migration, no secrets file: `git diff main...HEAD --name-only` has zero priv/repo/migrations/*.exs and zero config/*.exs entries).

CENTRAL QUESTION -- are the two new PUBLIC @doc false seams (run_script_sync/3, run_with_heap_limit_sync/4) an acceptable risk as shipped: YES, acceptable, for four independent reasons, and the design's rejection of a @compile-guarded/test-env-only definition is ALSO sound from a security standpoint specifically (not just ergonomics), for a fifth reason. (1) No production call path reaches them -- grepped the entire lib/ tree (`grep -rn "run_script_sync|run_with_heap_limit_sync" lib/`) and the ONLY hit outside executor.ex itself is the design doc; grepped the whole repo and the only caller anywhere is test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs. Neither function is referenced by the module's @behaviour (Letflow.Engine.LuaScriptAudit.Executor, @impl only on execute_with_manifest/2), by any router, any Oban worker, any process_instance/gen_statem callback, or any other lib/ module -- there is no reachable production entry point that would invoke them today. (2) A future non-test caller mistaking them for the normal entry point is a real but bounded and well-mitigated risk, not eliminated: @doc false hides them from generated docs and from `h Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor` in iex, but does not prevent direct qualified-call misuse by a future ELIXIR-DEV who greps the module and finds a same-arity-shaped sibling. What actually mitigates this: (a) both functions carry >30-line doc comments directly above their definitions naming them test-only, explaining WHY (categorical vs contractual guarantee, ISS-0426 provenance) and WHAT BREAKS if misused (unbounded hang for the heap-limited seam) -- a future reader who opens the source (which a qualified call requires finding first) cannot miss the warning; it is not a bare one-line comment, matching the handoff's own framing of the risk and clearing it; (b) the naming (_sync suffix, mirroring no existing production naming convention in this module) reads as deliberately test-flavored, unlike a plausible production name; (c) both functions produce IDENTICAL result shapes to their production counterparts on every branch except the removed wallclock_timeout error, so a mistaken call would not corrupt data or bypass tenant isolation even if it happened -- the worst case is DEGRADED AVAILABILITY (a hang, or a missing timeout enforcement for one call), not a confidentiality or integrity breach, which matters for severity calibration. (3) The precedent (build_script_error/3, executor.ex:438-457, cited by the design) is real and directly comparable: this module already carries a public @doc false test-only seam with the exact same risk shape, pre-dating this change, and no incident or finding exists against it -- checked via `git log` awareness is out of scope here but the code as it stands today already accepted this pattern once. (4) Blast radius if the theoretical misuse DID happen: since only tenant-authored SCRIPTS pass through this module (the caller, e.g. a workflow engine invocation, is always Letflow's own code, never tenant-supplied), a hypothetical production caller of run_script_sync/3 would still route every tenant script through Sandbox.new(max_instructions: budget) -- the instruction-budget enforcement (REQ-154) is NOT bypassed by either seam, only the wall-clock kill (LUA-10) is. A script that cannot escape the instruction counter (per the categorical-guarantee analysis, confirmed by direct read of run_script/3 at executor.ex:405-419: `Sandbox.new(max_instructions: budget)` is a real argument passed into the sandbox on every call, with no seam-specific exception) is still meaningfully bounded even via the unsafe seam for the nil-heap case -- it is only the small residual class of pcall-trap-and-loop scripts, specifically for the heap-limited path, where a genuine hang is possible, and even then the blast radius is a hung Elixir process, not data exposure. On the design's own rejection of a @compile-guard/Mix.env()==:test gate (§2.1.1a comparison table only mentions this negatively via the ergonomics framing per the task's pointer -- re-checked the full design doc for an explicit treatment of this specific alternative and found none beyond what the task description itself summarizes): judged from a SECURITY standpoint specifically, the rejection is ALSO sound, for a reason distinct from ergonomics -- a compile-time-conditional definition (`if Mix.env() == :test do ... end` around the def) is NOT actually a stronger security boundary than @doc false plus a doc comment for THIS threat model, because the threat this control matters against is a future INTERNAL developer/agent mis-wiring a call, not an external tenant reaching the function directly (tenant scripts execute inside the Lua VM sandbox itself and have no mechanism to call arbitrary BEAM-side Elixir functions by name -- that would require a capability-escape from the Lua sandbox, which is a wholly different and far more severe vulnerability class than anything this diff touches, and no such escape exists in this diff or is claimed to). A Mix.env() gate would additionally introduce a NEW risk this diff currently avoids: it would make the function's very existence conditional on compile-time environment, which is a well-known footgun for `mix compile` in :dev/:prod silently producing an UndefinedFunctionError if a test-tagged block anywhere ever gets exercised outside :test (a class of defect distinct from and arguably worse than the one being guarded against, since it would surface as a crash rather than a silent semantic gap). @doc false plus a substantial usage-contract comment is the right-sized control for an internal-developer-discipline risk with a bounded, availability-only (never confidentiality/integrity) blast radius -- CONFIRMED sufficient, not merely accepted for ergonomic convenience.

run_with_heap_limit_sync/4's UNBOUNDED WAIT (task item 2): confirmed via direct read (executor.ex:601-660) that max_heap_size: %{kill: true} is retained in the spawn_opt call, byte-identical to run_with_heap_limit/5's own spawn_opt (line 550 vs line 611 in the new function) -- REQ-156/LUA-09's memory bound is NOT weakened; only the caller's own wall-clock patience is removed. The availability risk (unbounded hang) is real and correctly NOT dismissed by the design -- but a documented usage contract is adequate specifically BECAUSE these are test-only entry points with a closed, enumerable caller set (verified: exactly 3 call sites, all inside test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs, all passing @moderate_allocating_script or @gigabyte_allocating_script -- both fixed-iteration loops with no pcall-trap-and-loop construct, confirmed by reading the scripts' literal source at executor_test.exs, matching the design's own §2.1.2a claim). A contract is NOT adequate for a production entry point with an open, unenumerable caller set and real tenant input -- the distinction the handoff asks to judge -- but this is the closed-caller-set case: worst-case failure of a contract violation here is a hung ExUnit test process, backstopped by ExUnit's own 60s default test timeout (an external bound this module doesn't need to provide itself), not a hung production request serving live tenant traffic. If a THIRD test call site were added later passing an unbounded-pcall-trap workload, the failure mode is a slow/hung CI run (loud, immediately visible, blocks the PR) -- not a silent production incident. Adequate for this scope; would NOT be adequate if either seam were ever exposed outside test/.

TEST WIRING (task's second concern -- tests silently stopping running anywhere): independently re-derived, not accepted. `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` (run fresh, this session) -> `Result: 37 passed, 11 excluded`. `mix test --only lua_wallclock_race test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` (run fresh, this session) -> `Result: 11 passed, 37 excluded` -- the two counts are exactly complementary (37+11=48 total, matching ORCH's pre-change baseline of 48), confirming the 11 tagged tests are neither lost nor duplicated, and that they genuinely execute and pass their timeout assertions in the isolated partition rather than being silently skipped forever. `grep -c '@tag :lua_wallclock_race' test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` = 11, matching both counts. CI CHAIN independently re-walked: .github/workflows/ci.yml's `backend` job runs `mix letflow.check` (confirmed by direct read of the workflow file) -> mix.exs's aliases block (`"letflow.check": [...]`, confirmed by direct read) ends its list with `"letflow.check.test"` -> lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex's diff (confirmed by direct read of the full diff) adds `run_lua_wallclock_race_tests()` as a new call inside `run/1`'s existing success-path `case`/`cond` branch, immediately after the pre-existing `run_wasm_hang_tests()` call, with zero lines removed or modified elsewhere in the file (git diff shows only `+` lines plus one `+` insertion into the existing success branch) -- the wiring is correct and CI does reach these 11 tests every run, isolated, via a subprocess whose exit code gates the task's own success (`if race_exit_code != 0 do Mix.raise(...)`, read directly). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (run fresh, this session): clean, zero output, exit 0.

No tenant-data path, no API route, no migration, no secrets handling touched by this change -- confirmed (not assumed) via `git diff main...HEAD --name-only`: 17 files total, all either handoffs/docs/design-doc bookkeeping, or the four files named in scope (executor.ex, executor_test.exs, test_helper.exs, letflow.check.test.ex). Zero priv/repo/migrations/*.exs, zero config/*.exs, zero web/ or API route files.
